en: 1. The Question of the Gourd Vine “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘one quality of the gourd vine should be adopted,’ which is that one quality that should be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, the gourd vine climbs up upon grass, wood, or another creeper by clinging with its tendrils and grows over it;”
In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga who desires to advance toward Arhatship should take hold of an object with the mind and advance toward Arhatship.
This, Great King, is one quality that should be adopted from the gourd vine.
And this, Great King, was said by the Elder Sāriputta, the General of the Dhamma:
"Just as one might grasp a gourd vine,
or grass, or wood, or a creeper,
in the same way, by a son of the Buddha who desires the fruit of Arhatship,
"Having taken an object as a support,
it should be developed toward the fruit of one beyond training (asekkhaphala).
Thus ends the first question on the gourd-stalk.
